summary: Redwood and Argent Trust reviewed incident response, BCDR (RTO/RPO), SLA/uptime guarantees, and escalation processes. Conversation covered SOC 2/ISO evidence, RBAC/SSO integration, audit logs retention, data residency constraints, and KMS/encryption options. Redwood proposed RTO targets with multi-region failover, described canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller model variants. Next steps include sharing SOC 2 artifacts, SLA appendix, and scheduling a tabletop drill.
topics: Incident response workflow and escalation matrix
BCDR strategy: RTO and RPO expectations, multi-region failover
Uptime / SLA commitments and historical uptime data
SOC 2 / ISO evidence and audit log samples
Encryption at rest and KMS integration (bring-your-own-key)
Data residency and private deployment options
transcript:
00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we have about 50 minutes, agenda is incident response, bcdr, sla and escalation. Marcus?
00:12 Marcus Lee: Thanks Alex, yep, appreciate it. we're evaluating Redwood for core customer-facing inference, so we need to understand your incident and b c d r posture, r t o r p o targets, and how escalation works.
00:25 Alex Kim: Great. Priya will lead the infra bits. Priya over to you.
00:30 Priya Shah: Hey team. quick note before i start—apologies, my connection is a little spotty, so if audio drops i'll rejoin. okay, on incident response we have a standard runbook that maps severity levels to response times, page routing, and cross-team escalation. For sev-1 we aim for acknowledgement within 15 minutes, initial mitigation steps in 30, and a bridge within 60. Our internal target r t o depends on failure mode—for regional outage with automatic failover we aim for an application-level r t o of under 5 minutes for critical routes, practical r t p o is near zero for stateless inference because of KV cache rebuild tradeoffs.
01:12 Diana Ortiz: sorry can i clarify—when you say KV cache rebuild, do you mean the K V in-memory cache for context? if that rebuilds it could add minutes to tail latency.
01:22 Priya Shah: yes correct—the KV cache rebuild cost can increase cold-start token latency; we use prefix caching and warmers to reduce that impact. for stateful sessions we have strategies to persist session context to a customer-managed store if required.
01:36 Evan Chen: can you explain persistence? Argent prefers not to have us hold PHI in app memory.
01:41 Priya Shah: absolutely. you can opt for private deployment + customer KMS; we also support session persistence to your VPC-managed Redis or object store. encryption at rest is standard and we support bring-your-own-key with HSM-backed KMS for private.
01:54 Marcus Lee: SOC 2 and ISO — what evidence can you provide? we need Type II and the last penetration test summary.
02:02 Alex Kim: we can provide SOC 2 type II report, iso attestation summary, and pen test executive summary under NDA. Priya will share redacted audit logs example so you can validate retention windows.
02:12 Sonia Patel: on legal side we'll need proof of data residency and contract language for breach notification timelines.
02:18 Alex Kim: understood. we include a breach notification clause and 72 hour window by contract; we'll share the specific language.
02:24 Noah Rivera: on escalation—we map severity to tiered contacts: SRE oncall -> infra leads -> engineering manager -> SE lead -> exec. for enterprise we add a VIP channel and a named account exec. escalation goes through pager duty integration and we can hook into your SSO for controlled access.
02:45 Diana Ortiz: SSO—how mature is your SAML / OIDC support and provisioning? we use Okta SCIM.
02:51 Priya Shah: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC via groups, and can map Okta groups to Redwood roles (admin, dev, read-only). some of the provisioning is manual initially but we can automate via SCIM.
03:06 Marcus Lee: retention windows for audit logs? we need at least 12 months online and 7 years cold archive for certain regs.
03:13 Priya Shah: default retention is 90 days online; we offer extended retention tiers to 3 years, and we can broker long-term archive with object storage in your cloud for 7+ years. logs include request/response metadata but not full prompt content by default unless requested and contracted.
03:29 Evan Chen: when you say request/response metadata, is there PII or prompt content stored?
03:33 Priya Shah: prompt content is redacted by default; we can enable full content retention under strict controls and encrypt using your KMS.
03:40 Marcus Lee: about RTO/RPO—can you walk through a multi-region outage scenario and how autoscaling and failover play?
03:48 Priya Shah: sure. in hosted mode we run active-passive across regions; traffic is routed via our edge layer and DNS failover with health checks. typical failover sequence: detect region down via synthetic checks (30-60s), route traffic to secondary region, spin up capacity if needed—if we have Dedicated reserved capacity in the secondary, failover can be sub-2 minutes; otherwise cold spin might be 3-7 minutes depending on model size and quantization. for RPO we rely on stateless inference for most flows so RPO is effectively zero; for persistent KV we recommend geo-replication of your store to minimize data loss window.
04:30 Marcus Lee: so realistic r t o numbers are 2 minutes with pre-warmed dedicated pools, 5-7 minutes without. is that fair?
04:37 Priya Shah: yes that's the ballpark. we also support warm standby policies and we can provision cross-region reserved capacity for critical SLAs.
04:44 Diana Ortiz: what's your SLA uptime percentage and credit policy?
04:47 Alex Kim: our enterprise SLA is 99.95% monthly for Dedicated with credits on a sliding scale. we'll send the precise appendix; historically our platform averages 99.99% across the last 12 months for customer-facing APIs, but specifics depend on account configuration.
04:59 Marcus Lee: escalation timeline—if a sev1 event continues beyond 4 hours who gets looped in?
05:05 Noah Rivera: after initial SRE engagement at 0-1 hour, at 4 hours we bring in infra leads and the SE. at 8 hours we escalate to engineering management and at 12 hours to execs. if contractual VIP, exec is looped earlier. we also perform RCA within 5 business days and a postmortem shared within 7 business days.
05:27 Evan Chen: do you provide runbooks for customer side as well? we want step-by-step actions for our ops.
05:32 Priya Shah: yes we provide a co-owned incident runbook and a customer playbook that outlines who does what in initial mitigation, who toggles DNS, and how to cut traffic to dedicated region. we'll draft an Argent-specific excerpt.
05:45 Marcus Lee: can you show an example of audit logs and retention schema?
05:49 Priya Shah: i'll share a redacted sample; note transcription might show some chars wrong in the logs but fields include timestamp, request_id, model_id, route, user_id (if provided), and anonymized prompt hash.
06:02 Diana Ortiz: data residency: Argent requires EU-only processing for EU customers. can we get a private deployment in our Paris region?
06:09 Alex Kim: we offer Private deployments and VPC options; for strict residency we can run a private control plane and optionally an on-prem inference cluster. deployment timelines and pricing differ, we'll outline in the follow-up.
06:20 Sonia Patel: about encryption—do you support BYOK and HSM integration?
06:24 Priya Shah: yes BYOK and HSM-backed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports customer-managed keys in our KMS federation model with restricted key import.
06:33 Marcus Lee: any SOC 2 findings historically we should be aware of?
06:36 Alex Kim: nothing material; minor findings around configuration hardening were closed in last quarter. we'll include the remediation timeline in the package.
06:44 Evan Chen: we run routine tabletop drills. can Redwood join and provide attack-injection scenarios?
06:49 Noah Rivera: yes we can participate; typically we simulate region failover, model regression and a credential compromise scenario. we can run a 2-hour tabletop with playbook review.
07:00 Diana Ortiz: can you describe your on-call rotation and SLAs for pagers? we want to mirror some of your expectations.
07:06 Priya Shah: our SREs are in 24/7 rotation with escalation to infra leads; typical acknowledgement SLA 15 minutes for sev1, follow-ups as previously described. we can exchange on-call rosters under NDA.
07:18 Marcus Lee: what's the process for security incidents that involve potential customer data exfiltration?
07:23 Alex Kim: we have a dedicated incident response team, we follow legal notification windows, we preserve forensic evidence, and engage third-party forensics for high-severity breaches. contractual breach notification is within 72 hours; we'll provide the exact playbook.
07:36 Sonia Patel: for contract language we need sample clauses for breach notification, data processing agreement, and subprocessor list.
07:42 Alex Kim: we'll share DPA and subprocessor list.
07:45 Evan Chen: on RPO for session state, if we use customer-managed redis geo-replicated, what is the expected RPO?
07:52 Priya Shah: that depends on your replication lag; under synchronous replication it's near zero, async it's bounded by replication lag which you should measure; we recommend sync or semi-sync for critical flows.
08:05 Marcus Lee: can you run a small benchmark for failover times with a 13B quantized model?
08:11 Priya Shah: yes—we can run a targeted failover benchmark from eu-west to eu-central using a representative payload; that'll show cold spin times and kv warm-up. Noah will own that.
08:21 Noah Rivera: noted, i'll coordinate with Evan on test harness.
08:24 Diana Ortiz: about monitoring and traces—do you provide per-request traces and token-level timings?
08:29 Priya Shah: yes, per-request latency breakdown, token times, model queue time, and per-route metrics in the console; you can stream traces to your datadog or prometheus endpoints.
08:40 Marcus Lee: do you keep a history of incidents and RCA?
08:43 Alex Kim: yes, we maintain incident history, RCA documents, and we can share a sanitized list of incidents and learnings for evaluation.
08:51 Evan Chen: what's the expected lead time to provision cross-region reserved capacity?
08:55 Alex Kim: usually 2-4 weeks to provision and test, faster for accounts with committed contracts.
09:02 Sonia Patel: if we require 7-year archives for logs, is there any cost or compliance impact?
09:08 Priya Shah: we'll use your cloud object storage; cost is storage + retrieval; we can produce a cost estimate in the follow-up.
09:14 Marcus Lee: any blocker for SOC 2 plus data residency?
09:17 Alex Kim: no blockers; private deployment or dedicated capacity in your region addresses residency, and SOC 2 artifacts cover controls. we'll produce a deployment plan.
09:25 Diana Ortiz: about escalation channels—do you have an official VIP slack channel or dedicated email?
09:29 Noah Rivera: we support VIP channels, dedicated slack workspaces, and a phone escalation tree—configured per account.
09:37 Evan Chen: ok let's recap next steps.
09:40 Alex Kim: recap: we'll share SOC 2, pen test summary, audit log sample, SLA appendix, and runbook excerpt. schedule tabletop drill week of 11/2. Noah and Evan will coordinate the failover benchmark. any other asks?
09:56 Marcus Lee: please include the legal clauses and subprocessor list.
09:59 Sonia Patel: and a contact list for on-call.
10:03 Alex Kim: got it. thanks all, we'll follow up by email and set the next meeting.
10:08 Diana Ortiz: thanks everyone.
10:12 (call ends)
notes: Customer strongly prioritizes EU data residency and 7-year archive for logs
RTO targets discussed: ~2 min with pre-warmed dedicated, 5-7 min cold spin
Argent requests SOC 2 Type II report, pen-test summary, SLA appendix, and incident runbook excerpt
